Gathering Flowers for the Master's Bouquet

liner.body_md:
## What listeners single out

- **Dark Star//** (2 reviews, 1 other source): The reviewer says the jam only heated up in the second half of the piece; Mellow, laid-back version where wind chimes are more audible than on any other Dark Star the reviewer knows [1][4][14]
- **//New Speedway Boogie** (2 reviews): Reviewer found it great, while judging Dark Star underwhelming; The cut at the end of Dark Star carries into this, which has unusual backing vocals [8][11]
- **Uncle John's Band** (1 review): Described as semi-electric, and the acoustic set is highlighted by a nice Black Peter [11]
- **Turn On Your Love Light** (1 review): Reviewer found it solid but too short, preferring much longer versions of around twenty-five minutes [4]

## Setlist highlights

- **Little Sadie**: rare: 7 archived performances [16]
- **Long Black Limousine**: rare: 4 archived performances [16]
- **All Around This World**: rare: 7 archived performances [16]
- **The Master's Bouquet**: earliest performance in the archive; legendary: the only archived performance [16]
- **drum tuning/**: earliest performance in the archive; legendary: the only archived performance [16]
- **stage announcment**: earliest performance in the archive; mythic rare: 2 archived performances [16]

## The recordings

- **gd1969-12-26.sbd.warner-evans.28448.sbeok.flac16** (recommended): soundboard; 20 songs; 124 min; rated 4.2/5 by 15 [1]
- **gd69-12-26.sbd.murphy.1821.sbeok.shnf**: soundboard; 17 songs; 122 min; rated 4.24/5 by 25 [2]. Said about its sound: Recording cuts out during Cold Rain And Snow, and the start of China Cat Sunflower is chopped; All circulating versions have cuts at the start of China Cat, end of Dark Star, and start of New Speedway Boogie [2][6]
- **gd1969-12-26.136636.electric.sbd.mr.cass.sirmick.flac1648**: soundboard; 10 songs; 79 min; rated 2/5 by 2 [3]

## Around the show

- Billy arrived late, so Bobby and Jerry opened with old acoustic standards before the electric portion [4]
- Bill was late, apparently because of Christmas the day before, which led to an unexpected acoustic opening set [5]
- The band played acoustic gospel and country standards while waiting for the late drummer to arrive [6]
- Reviewer considers this the first official public acoustic Dead performance, since Billy ran late; electric portion is slow to get going [7]
- The audience sounds polite on the tape, reminiscent of some Europe '72 shows [8]
- Reviewer's first concert at age 14; parents dropped them off at SMU, and the experience changed their worldview [12]
- The show was reportedly a stopover on the trip from California to the East Coast [14]
- Both this show and the Fillmore show on the 29th are said to be the first acoustic show because Bill was late [9]
- Per Deadbase, a four-song acoustic set on 12/19 came first, but this one is longer and better [11]
- The April 5th 1969 Avalon show also opened acoustically, with Dupree's into Mountains and Jerry singing Mountains [13]

## Tapers and lineage

- **gd1969-12-26.sbd.warner-evans.28448.sbeok.flac16**: transferred by Jack Warner, Marc Evans, Jim Powell; source: MSR> CASS> DAT> CDR> EAC> FLAC [1]. Also: This version repairs Cold Rain And Snow and China Cat Sunflower cuts using a second-generation cassette source [1]
- **gd69-12-26.sbd.murphy.1821.sbeok.shnf**: transferred by Bob Murphy; source: Soundboard [2]
- **gd1969-12-26.136636.electric.sbd.mr.cass.sirmick.flac1648**: taped by Anonomous; transferred by SIRMick; source: flac16/48kHz ; Set 2 Source: sbd > Master Reel > Cassette > Dat (48k) [3]

## Art and photos

- Poster by gocollect.com: [Grateful Dead SMU McFarlin Auditorium 1969 Value - GoCollect](https://gocollect.com/concert-poster/grateful-dead-at-smu-mcfarlin-auditorium-1969) [17]
